Description: NudgeBee Scenario Lab - services tier. Four hosts running an order/payment/inventory application over PostgreSQL, wired so a failure in one genuinely breaks the others. Deploy the lab tier first; this reuses its VPC, security group and instance profile.

LabStackName.Description: Lab-tier stack whose network and instance profile these hosts reuse.

InstanceType.Description: t3.micro is tight once PostgreSQL is on the box.

DetailedMonitoring.Description: One-minute EC2 metrics alongside the per-minute service health metric.

#!/bin/bash
set -x
dnf install -y postgresql15-server postgresql15 awscli-2 cronie || yum install -y postgresql-server postgresql cronie || true
systemctl enable --now crond || true
PGSETUP_INITDB_OPTIONS="--auth-host=md5" postgresql-setup --initdb || true
PGDATA=$(ls -d /var/lib/pgsql/*/data 2>/dev/null | head -1)
[ -z "$PGDATA" ] && PGDATA=/var/lib/pgsql/data
sed -i "s/^#*listen_addresses.*/listen_addresses = '*'/" "$PGDATA/postgresql.conf"
grep -q 'nudgebee-scenario-lab' "$PGDATA/pg_hba.conf" || echo "host all all 10.42.0.0/16 md5  # nudgebee-scenario-lab" >> "$PGDATA/pg_hba.conf"
systemctl enable --now postgresql
sleep 5
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE USER labapp WITH PASSWORD 'labapp';" || true
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE DATABASE labdb OWNER labapp;" || true
sudo -u postgres psql -d labdb -c "CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS orders (id serial primary key, note text);" || true
sudo -u postgres psql -d labdb -c "INSERT INTO orders (note) SELECT 'seed' WHERE NOT EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM orders);" || true
# The table is created by the postgres superuser, so labapp owns the database
# but not the table inside it - the app connects fine and then cannot read.
sudo -u postgres psql -d labdb -c "ALTER TABLE orders OWNER TO labapp;" || true
sudo -u postgres psql -d labdb -c "GRANT ALL ON SCHEMA public TO labapp;" || true
sudo -u postgres psql -d labdb -c "GRANT ALL ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA public TO labapp;" || true

cat >/usr/local/bin/nb-health.sh <<'HEALTH'
#!/bin/bash
ROLE="$1"; PORT="$2"
# Amazon Linux 2023 enforces IMDSv2, so an unauthenticated metadata GET
# returns 401 and REGION ends up empty - which fails as
# "Invalid endpoint: https://monitoring..amazonaws.com" and publishes nothing,
# leaving every alarm breaching on missing data. CloudFormation knows the
# region, so take it from there and skip the metadata service entirely.
REGION="${AWS::Region}"
# IMDSv2 is enforced on AL2023 - an unauthenticated GET returns 401, so the
# token call is required, not optional.
IMDS_TOKEN=$(curl -s -m 3 -X PUT "http://169.254.169.254/latest/api/token" -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token-ttl-seconds: 300")
IID=$(curl -s -m 3 -H "X-aws-ec2-metadata-token: $IMDS_TOKEN" http://169.254.169.254/latest/meta-data/instance-id)
if [ "$ROLE" = "database" ]; then
  pg_isready -q -h 127.0.0.1 && UP=1 || UP=0
else
  code=$(curl -s -m 5 -o /dev/null -w '%{http_code}' "http://127.0.0.1:${!PORT}/health")
  [ "$code" = "200" ] && UP=1 || UP=0
fi
# InstanceId matters as much as the value. Without it the event NudgeBee
# builds has subject_type "alarm" and subject_name "order", resolving to no
# cloud resource - so no graph node, no correlation and no analysis. With it
# the event resolves to the EC2 instance, exactly like a native alarm does.
aws cloudwatch put-metric-data --region "$REGION" \
  --namespace NudgebeeScenarioLab --metric-name ServiceHealthy \
  --dimensions InstanceId="$IID" --value "$UP" --unit None
HEALTH
chmod +x /usr/local/bin/nb-health.sh
cat >/etc/systemd/system/nb-health.service <<UNIT
[Unit]
Description=NudgeBee scenario lab health metric
[Service]
Type=oneshot
ExecStart=/usr/local/bin/nb-health.sh database 0
UNIT
cat >/etc/systemd/system/nb-health.timer <<'TIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Publish service health every minute
[Timer]
OnBootSec=90
# OnUnitInactiveSec, not OnUnitActiveSec. This service is Type=oneshot: it runs
# for under a second and exits, so "60s after it became active" never produces
# a next trigger and the timer fires exactly once, then shows NEXT as blank.
# Measuring from when it went inactive is what actually repeats.
OnUnitInactiveSec=60
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
TIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now nb-health.timer

#!/bin/bash
set -x
dnf install -y python3 postgresql15 awscli-2 cronie || yum install -y python3 postgresql cronie || true
systemctl enable --now crond || true

# /health is what makes the cascade real: it returns 200 only when this
# service's own upstreams answer, so stopping an upstream genuinely fails
# everything downstream of it instead of us faking three alerts.

cat >/opt/nb-service.py <<'APPPY'
import os, subprocess, urllib.request
from http.server import BaseHTTPRequestHandler, HTTPServer

ROLE = os.environ.get("NB_ROLE", "service")
PORT = int(os.environ.get("NB_PORT", "8080"))
UPSTREAMS = [u for u in os.environ.get("NB_UPSTREAMS", "").split(",") if u]
DB_HOST = os.environ.get("NB_DB_HOST", "")

def db_ok():
    if not DB_HOST:
        return True
    env = dict(os.environ, PGPASSWORD="labapp", PGCONNECT_TIMEOUT="3")
    try:
        r = subprocess.run(["psql", "-h", DB_HOST, "-U", "labapp", "-d", "labdb",
                            "-tAc", "select count(*) from orders"],
                           capture_output=True, timeout=6, env=env)
        return r.returncode == 0
    except Exception:
        return False

def upstreams_ok():
    for u in UPSTREAMS:
        try:
            with urllib.request.urlopen("http://%s/health" % u, timeout=4) as r:
                if r.status != 200:
                    return False, u
        except Exception:
            return False, u
    return True, ""

class H(BaseHTTPRequestHandler):
    def do_GET(self):
        if self.path.startswith("/health"):
            up_ok, bad = upstreams_ok()
            d_ok = db_ok()
            body = "service=%s upstreams_ok=%s db_ok=%s" % (ROLE, up_ok, d_ok)
            if not up_ok:
                body += " failing_upstream=%s" % bad
            self.send_response(200 if (up_ok and d_ok) else 503)
        else:
            self.send_response(200)
            body = "service=%s" % ROLE
        self.send_header("Content-Type", "text/plain")
        self.end_headers()
        self.wfile.write((body + "\n").encode())
    def log_message(self, *a):
        pass

HTTPServer(("0.0.0.0", PORT), H).serve_forever()
APPPY

cat >/etc/systemd/system/order.service <<UNIT
[Unit]
Description=order service (NudgeBee scenario lab)
After=network-online.target
[Service]
Environment=NB_ROLE=order
Environment=NB_PORT=8081
Environment=NB_UPSTREAMS=
Environment=NB_DB_HOST=${DbIp}
ExecStart=/usr/bin/python3 /opt/nb-service.py
Restart=always
RestartSec=5
[Install]
WantedBy=multi-user.target
UNIT
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now order

# Steady calls to upstreams. This is the traffic the VPC flow-log service map
# is built from - with no calls between hosts the graph has nothing to see.
echo "NB_UPSTREAMS=" > /etc/nb-traffic.env
cat >/etc/systemd/system/nb-traffic.service <<'UNIT'
[Unit]
Description=Steady call traffic to upstreams
[Service]
Type=oneshot
EnvironmentFile=/etc/nb-traffic.env
ExecStart=/bin/bash -c 'for u in $(echo "$NB_UPSTREAMS" | tr "," " "); do [ -n "$u" ] && curl -s -m 3 -o /dev/null "http://$u/health"; done'
UNIT
cat >/etc/systemd/system/nb-traffic.timer <<'TIMER'
[Unit]
Description=Call upstreams every 15s
[Timer]
OnBootSec=100
OnUnitActiveSec=15
[Install]
WantedBy=timers.target
TIMER
systemctl daemon-reload
systemctl enable --now nb-traffic.timer
